item.title: The Amazing Digital Circus Finale Review
item.description:
Welcome To MediaPlay

Hey everyone and happy Friday! This is Crystal, the host of MediaPlay, where I cover what’s happening in the center of the digital entertainment world on the official website of BFM and also on Patreon!

I’ve just finished watching the final episode of 1The Amazing Digital Circus from both GLITCH Productions and Gooseworx, and it has been a big rollercoaster ride to the end of the series. So, I decided to do a full review of the finale, and there can be a few spoilers here. If you have not seen the episode, even though most have seen the episode in the form of The Last Act in the movie theater, check the finale on the GLITCH YouTube Channel and see it for yourself.

Enough talk, let’s dive right in and let’s play!

The Review of the Finale

As the box office has gotten GLITCH Productions worldwide with The Last Act screening of both Episodes 8 and 9, the finale has fully premiered on both YouTube and Netflix. By looking at the poster art and trailer for the finale, this episode is primarily focused on Jax and takes place after the events of the previous episode when Kinger accidentally purged Caine from the circus.

The reason this finale focuses on Jax is because he has a complicated past in his life at the circus and a friendship with Ribbit, one of the former circus members before she was abstracted. Plus, this is also the first time we see Kaufmo, before his abstraction, in the episode, as he was first mentioned in the pilot episode. Based on what I noticed in the finale, we didn’t actually see Jax abstracted with our own eyes at the first few minutes of the episode, as this was technically an off-screen moment.

Although, throughout the series, Jax’s behavior and actions are basically his misdemeanor of screwing around with the other circus members, in the finale, we get to see Jax’s vulnerability and personal conflict at the same time.

Despite of Kaufmo, Ribbit, and Jax’s downfall that led to their abstraction, the surviving members of the digital circus finally remembers their lives before the circus and also their real names after when Caine returned to allow them to have full control of the circus itself and live their lives to the fullest.

Aside, from the animation, this is also the first time that live action was used in a show by GLITCH as the post-credits revealed the real life versions of the main characters, which is very impressive.

The Media Verdict for the Finale

As the series ended with nine episodes in total, and also that the finale was mostly emotional for the characters including Jax’s final moments, me and the MediaPlay team gives the final episode of The Amazing Digital Circus with a rating of 9 out of 10 with an A grade.

There was one criticism I have in regards to the abstraction of Jax at the ending of the finale, why didn’t we saw him abstract early in the episode? Probably, that would been explanatory due to his mental state worsening throughout the series up until this point in the finale.

But at least the gang has their happy ending…especially Zooble and Gangle having their make out moment during the credits of the show, which should not be discussed in the workplace if you know what I mean.

Wrapping Up The Media

2By the time of the last modification date of this post, the cast of TADC shared their emotional moments and thanking the audience for their support to the show through a social media post by GLITCH.

Aside from the thanks by the cast, more posts related to the finale were everywhere including posts from the live action cast and Morgana Ignis, who is GLITCH’s Global Brand Manager, and also the VA who played Sallie Mae from Helluva Boss and Naki Kito from the English dub of DanDaDan.

On Google, by searching content related to the finale or maybe searching The Last Act, there is a easter egg that references the moment where Kinger was desperately trying to modify Caine’s code in Episode 8, which is pretty cool to spam the icons of Caine and Bubble across the search results.

So, to end off with the review, now that The Amazing Digital Circus has been concluded, whats going to happen next for GLITCH, there are three other shows that needs attention: Gameoverse, The Gaslight District, and Knights of Guinevere.

Will these shows be greenlitted to continue production? We will find out soon in the distant future for GLITCH and its showrunners.

That’s all we have to cover here! Thanks for reading MediaPlay from Benjamin Fernandez Media. See you on the next issue!

  1. The Amazing Digital Circus belongs to GLITCH Productions and Gooseworx ↩︎

  2. As of publishing this post with the updated date of June 20, 2026, the mentioned posts can be found anywhere online through official channels on social media. ↩︎

item.title: v3.0 - Welcome to Version 3.0!
item.description:
After a long development week or two to fix improvements in the overall website experience, it is my pleasure to announce that the website has been officially updated to Version 3.0! This update introduces some major changes to the site, including: a new ticker for MediaPlay, improvements to some icons and dark mode, and an updated layout for the home page!

As I continue to work on the website to add new features and pages, this can eventually be populated with more content, especially for the MediaPlay newsletter, but for now, let’s enjoy what we have in this major update and see what’s new on the official website of BFM!

New Features

Redesigned Home Layout

Before the redesign
After the redesign

After doing some research using the Developer Tools on Chrome, I paid close attention to the image classes that control how both light and dark versions of my logo are viewed when the theme is toggled or how the theme behaves based on how your system is configured for dark mode.

By using hx:hidden hx:dark:block for the dark logo and hx:block hx:dark:hidden for the light logo, the former text that represents the brand is now replaced with the logo to ensure that the brand is more recognizable! Plus, the icons for the Not By AI badge and the stuff I use to make the site and content have also been updated with their appropriate classes!

For the icons that displayed the skills I use to make the site, I performed some trial and error when programming the icons to switch from light to dark by adding an additional container for the light-themed icons and trying to hide them when the theme is toggled. However, it didn’t work until I found a solution.

Before the redesign
Before programming, all of the icons belonging to Skillsicon had a URL to target only that specific icon of choice. When toggling themes, these icons are not ‘dynamic’.
After the redesign
By adding another ‘img src’ tag into the existing link tag and the classes I used for the logo, when toggling between light or dark, the icons will change to their appropriate theme.

Meet The New MediaPlay Ticker

Have you noticed something different on the ticker that you always see on the home page? Well, that’s actually the MediaPlay ticker, where it displays all published articles from the newsletter, and guess what? The ticker has been redesigned from the ground up!

While the old version of the ticker is considered a prototype, there was an issue when the prototype of the ticker was used…it was not responsive on smaller devices. While facing some programming difficulty in retaining the size of the MediaPlay logo, some attempts were made to add a smaller version of the logo to ensure it’s simplified, but it underwent unsuccessful attempts due to the complexity of the classes I tried to use for the assets.

For this new ticker, with an additional container to show the logo and its brand-new tagline, the logo functionality remains the same. Clicking on the logo will take you to the MediaPlay page on the website. Also, note that this new ticker is responsive now, and it has been tested with no issues whatsoever.

Improvements and Fixes

Version 3.0 introduces the following fixes and improvements, that are aside from the new features that were disclosed in this post, but not limited to the following:

  • The RSS icon is now in the website’s main navigation bar for instant access to our main site’s RSS feed.
  • The icon for the MediaPlay link on the navigation bar was fixed. Originally, in the previous build, when toggling light theme on, you basically see a straight-up play icon while the ‘M’ inside the play icon is still black. By redoing the logo design on Figma, this icon has been fixed with the ‘M’ as a cutout!
  • Updated social links and added additional icons in the icons.yaml file that will eventually be used in the future.
  • Updated the Help and Information index page, replacing the image that was used on the homepage with the branding image that is used as our OpenGraph image.
  • Updated the 404 page; it may be a visual upgrade to align with our main brand’s tagline and theme.
  • Added fixed time zone as timeZone: 'America/New_York to fix the date and time on each blog post that is published to the site, and also updated the publishDate on every post.

Under The Code

When working on the idea to adapt the icons for both dark and light themes of the site, I discovered the classes that were part of the theme, as it uses Tailwind CSS as the prefix and utility classes. I originally thought those classes will apply to containers but it only works on images. Lesson learned!

item.title: Indie Animations Have Been Wildly Trending
item.description:
Welcome To MediaPlay

1Good evening, everyone! Welcome to our brand newsletter called MediaPlay, where I review the latest content and news related to what’s going on in the world of digital entertainment. My name is Crystal, and I am your main hostess of the newsletter here on the BFM website and also on Patreon, and this first issue is going to be packed with the recent indie animations that were published last week and have been getting popular with a wild trend around social media!

I have to say that last week has been crazy through the fandoms from both GLITCH Productions and the crazy gang over from SpindleHorse Toons with their shows on YouTube, Amazon Prime Video, and Netflix. For the center of it all, for last week, we have travelled back in time with a brand new pilot that came from the Y2K from artist and creator Rafael Andaya!

Before the MediaPlay team and I published our first issue, to review the content that was recently published, we were immediately stunned, or maybe flabbergasted by SpindleHorse, that the fans of one of their shows, Helluva Boss, expected a short related to one of the hot characters of the show, Verosika Mayday, until unfortunately we got Chaz’d…again! We’ll explain about that later in the issue. Enough intro! Time to dive right in and let’s play!

Returning To The Nostalgia With A New Pilot

Ah yes, the early 2000s…the millennium…we knew the vibes of early childhood were returning, but with an indie twist too! Last Monday, the fans and viewers of indie animation were stoked with a new pilot episode from artist and creator, Rafael Andaya, with their new show called 2PLANETRONIKA, an early-Y2K sci-fi comedy featuring two cool-looking characters that have been on the buzz throughout the week. What we have here is a sneak preview video of the pilot episode! Take a look!

Plot of the PLANETRONIKA Pilot Episode

Taking place on a fictional planet called Tereste with its early Y2K vibes, two friends named Butterfly and Freestyle decided to take a break from work and challenge each other with a game of basketball! Unfortunately, their usual game gets chaotic with a dribble malfunction as the ball goes haywire in their surroundings.

It’s not usual for a plot like this where a game of basketball gets deadly after one malfunction, but in the world of PLANETRONIKA, it takes a go of a misadventure with a big twist of millennium fun!

The pilot episode is filled with classic memes and references

Well then… it seems like this show has a lot of well-known memes and references from the early-2000s internet back in the day. For those who were born as Generation Z (people who were born in 2000), you may recognize some memes and references throughout the pilot episode, like the split-second troll face, the three guys on a planet (which I do not know the name of), and, of course, the Caramelldansen dance performed by Butterfly. Have you found them all in the episode?

The Media Verdict for PLANETRONIKA

Ayeiyaiya, I’m your little butterfly~ Oh, sorry! I zoned out a bit there. Y2K will always be embedded in the Generation Z DNA. Anyway, since the show had demonstrated the vibes of old-fashioned Y2K shows based on its look and feel on the world-building, characters, plot, and setting, MediaPlay gives Rafael Andaya’s PLANETRONIKA an 11 out of 10 with an average scale of A+! The extra point was given since a lot of detail and remembrance of nostalgia were put in during the making of the pilot episode!

To check out the full pilot episode of PLANETRONIKA, watch the full pilot only on YouTube!

Video Games Are Everything…But In A Deadly Twist

While 3GLITCH Productions is focusing on stuff related to the final episode of The Amazing Digital Circus and its theatrical debut for the premiere of both Episodes 8 and 9 across the world this summer, they have released a new show called Gameoverse that was created and directed by Ross O’Donovan, while Arin Hanson, who is famously known online as the co-host of Game Grumps on YouTube, co-written the show. This action-packed adventure consists of the idea of where video games meet the apocalypse, as each game world gets destroyed if that world doesn’t get saved in time.

As the show was released on Friday last week, that has been reports that fans were starting to see a bit of fan service from the episode since it was actually a beach episode, and then there was some backlash over the design choices for both Kit and Miss Information on numerous posts on Twitter.

Although the show looked pretty good, and the character designs and world-building have been put in a lot of hard work by the team over at GLITCH.

MEDIA BREAKING: TADC Episode 9 Got LEAKED!

What!? MediaPlay has started its first issue, and now we have breaking news already over The Amazing Digital Circus? Man, that was pretty fast!

Well then…this is surprisingly shocking, and also a big spoiler in a way, so by the time of posting our first issue, not too long ago, on YouTube through a post by Ayy Lmao, it was revealed that someone had leaked the final episode of TADC online before its theatrical release. As this sounds pretty bad, this will most likely spread everywhere online, and it can result in the leaks being removed by either GLITCH Productions or Gooseworx submitting a DMCA copyright takedown to avoid the leaks from spreading.

At MediaPlay, in my defense as a host, publishing unreleased material from an overrated show can lead to some spoilers, and people can have serious reactions to what the ending would be from the show. I advise not to look at the leaks that are spreading online and wait until the actual premiere of the final episode of TADC in your local movie theater, on YouTube, and potentially on Netflix.

The Fans of Helluva Boss Got Chaz’d…once again

I’m almost done here on this first issue, but now we are entering VivziePop territory as Friday is also marked with a new release of a 12th short, or basically a music video from SpindleHorse’s show, Helluva Boss. Originally, the social channels of 4SpindleHorse posted an image of what fans had assumed that the next short would involve, Verosika Mayday, due to the appearance of a character shown from an underwater perspective at a local pool.

However, that all changed when Eric Schwartz, the voice of Chaz, whose character had recently appeared in the April Fools short and in the earlier episodes of the show, posted on social media, sharing a hint that it’s not Verosika while he was swimming in a pool.

So it appears that Chaz or Zahc or whatever the F@#K his name is, was most likely to appear again for the new short. On the day of the shorts’ release, the entire HB fandom got flabbergasted by a new music video titled “Sharkboy Summer”.

In all honesty, I have confirmed in my suspicions that Chaz is NOT dead in a way, although he had his teeth ripped by Moxxie’s father in one of the episodes, which has been revealed in the previous short, and has shark dentures. But we will never know whether it’s actually him or his so-called twin brother, nor whether he is actually DEAD, that may not stop him from his game of being the most perverted character throughout the entire series. But that’s just my opinion in a way, not to be disrespectful to the show’s VAs and the main creator.

All I can say is that the funeral was basically a setup so that Chaz could fool everyone and get away with it, and probably gonna be continuing bragging about his big appendage. Obviously, that is the context of the music video, as this is technically a song of Chaz’s seductive territory. But to put this positively, it’s also to note that we get to see the Envy ring for the very first time. In all strong honesty, most people, including myself, had fair shares of seeing weird things around the internet and mostly stuff in the show, but this was WAYYYYYY overboard, so the short was too much Chaz, if you know what I mean.

Overall, aside from that seductive weirdo, we are still looking forward to the upcoming seasons of Helluva Boss and also the new seasons of Hazbin Hotel from SpindleHorse, which will be coming soon on YouTube and on Amazon Prime Video. Please continue to follow the social channels of SpindleHorse for more updates and details regarding the Helluvaverse.

Wrapping Up The Media

Well, that’s all we have for the first issue for tonight. Seems like the indie animation stuff has gone wild in a way, based on the context of the fandom and also the shorts, too. But for PLANETRONIKA, we may see more of that in the distant future and see how it goes for its development.

MediaPlay will have more content to cover real soon in the next issue, so stay tuned on the website and on Patreon to get the latest coverage of what’s going on in the digital entertainment world! Plus, we may start covering stuff related to gaming along the way, and some movie reviews based on interest.

Thanks for reading MediaPlay from Benjamin Fernandez Media! Good night, everyone!
